messages.subject: Re: Eigen Maps
parts:
The problem is that there's no way to create a std::vector<double>
out of a double* without copying the data. At least not without
a custom allocator. The underlying issue is that std::vector
wants to manage its own memory. Here are the constructors:

http://www.cplusplus.com/reference/vector/vector/vector/

You could use the .data() from a Matrix as an iterator.
With Eigen vectors, you know you'll get the data out in the
proper order.

An Eigen::Map just gives you a view into the data
array.

std::vector<double> v = ...;
double* dbl_ptr = &v[0];
Map<Matrix<double,Dynamic,1> > map_m(dbl_ptr);
m[1] = 2.0; // changes v

But as soon as you assign it, you lose the connection:

Matrix<double,Dynamic,1> m = map_m; // Copy!
map_m[1] = 3.0; // does not change v

You can even customize the stride in the Map in case
you have a 2D array laid out C++ style and you need
to use it in Eigen. Here's an overview:

http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/TutorialMapClass.html

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Eigen Maps
parts:
n 3/20/13 8:46 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> Gah, I was hoping to use Eigen exclusively for all of the internals and just wrap the calls to prob_grad with maps. I guess I have to rethink some code.

I don't see the problem -- just map the input std::vector
into the appropriate Eigen vector, use that, then copy
the output into another std::vector for output.

We should've made the arguments to log_prob_grad const.
The obstacle to refactoring now is the io::reader, which should
be modified to read from a const reference.

We should just refactor the whole framework to take an Eigen
vector as input and produce sample objects with Eigen
vectors. I do not think these should be mutable.

- Bob
